=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py | `_run_poller_subprocess`, lines 384-391 (the new wait loop) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The poller subprocess is launched with `start_new_session=True` (line 355), making `proc.pid` the process-group ID. After `os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)`, the child processes in the group die but become zombies until reaped. Because the test process is not the parent of those descendants (the main child was, and `proc.communicate()` already reaped the main child), the zombies are reparented to init/subreaper but remain in the process group. `os.killpg(proc.pid, 0)` succeeds as long as any process (including zombies) exists in the group, so `ProcessLookupError` is not raised until init reaps them. The loop therefore runs the full 1-second deadline on nearly every non-crash exit.
  WHY: Each poller subprocess test now pays up to ~1 second of wall time even on the success path. The module has many tests that spawn the poller, and CI shards them across 4 local workers per matrix group. The bounded wait prevents the `[Errno 39] Directory not empty` race the change targets, but the fixed 1-second cost per subprocess is a measurable test-runtime regression. A short fixed sleep (e.g., 0.1-0.2s) would cover the detach window for git auto-gc without polling the full deadline, or the loop could call `os.waitpid(-proc.pid, os.WNOHANG)` to reap zombies in the group and let the group dissolve sooner.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
